page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. The instance configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with multithreading, along with 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A 236 GB NVMe SSD is bundled for fast local scratch storage. Accelerated matrix and vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8) are present on the host CPU. There are no discrete GPUs allocated.

Benchmark outcomes show dependable single-threaded capability alongside aggregate multithreaded constraints expected from a 4-vCPU machine. Single-threaded gzip compression scored in the upper 25% at 31.35 GB/sec, while Geekbench single-core performance reached 1643.0 and stress-ng recorded 1948.38, placing both in the median tier. Multithreaded workloads fell into lower tiers relative to broader cloud environments, reflecting the physical 2-core boundary. Memory read bandwidth measured 36.24 GB/sec for uncached 256MB blocks, with write bandwidth registering at 25.93 GB/sec.

Given its high RAM-to-CPU ratio and fast bundled NVMe disk, the E4ds_v6 offers strong resource density for memory-centric software without the overhead of massive compute core allocations. It is well suited for relational and in-memory databases, intermediate cache nodes, data analysis pipelines, and general memory-bound business applications.
